title: State Spectral Gap
label: thm:spectrum
statement: [State Spectral Gap] Fix u in U in the typed computable model. Assume T_u is Fr 'echet differentiable at its fixed point f_u^ ast . Then [ rho ! left (DT_u(f_u^ ast ) right ) le norm DT_u(f_u^ ast ) le norm widetilde K le frac 1 2 . ] Consequently the state spectral gap satisfies [ Delta _ mathrm state ge 1- norm widetilde K ge frac 1 2 . ]
statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[State Spectral Gap]\label{thm:spectrum}
Fix $u\in\U$ in the typed computable model. Assume $T_u$ is Fr\'echet differentiable at its fixed point $f_u^\ast$. Then
\[
\rho\!\left(DT_u(f_u^\ast)\right)
\le
\norm{DT_u(f_u^\ast)}
\le
\norm{\widetilde K}
\le
\frac{1}{2}.
\]
Consequently the state spectral gap satisfies
\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{state}}\ge 1-\norm{\widetilde K}\ge \frac{1}{2}.
\]
\end{theorem}

title: NFD: Non-Finite Determination
label: hyp:nfd
statement: [NFD: Non-Finite Determination] For every t in mathbb N , the canonical projection [ p_t: Id to S_t, qquad p_t((x_k)_k)=x_t ] is not injective. Equivalently, [ forall t exists x,y in Id quad x neq y quad text and quad p_t(x)=p_t(y). ]
statement_tex:
\begin{hypothesis}[NFD: Non-Finite Determination]\label{hyp:nfd}
For every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the canonical projection
\[
p_t:\Id\to S_t,
\qquad
p_t((x_k)_k)=x_t
\]
is not injective. Equivalently,
\[
\forall t\ \exists x,y\in\Id
\quad
x\neq y
\quad\text{and}\quad
p_t(x)=p_t(y).
\]
\end{hypothesis}

title: Persistent future branching as an operational form of NFD
statement: [Persistent future branching as an operational form of NFD] A sufficient operational strengthening of Hypothesis~ ref hyp:nfd is: for every t there exists k>t and x_t in S_t such that the fiber of pi _ k to t over x_t contains at least two globally extendable compatible histories. BaseCore keeps the weaker NFD statement as the primary assumption because it is exactly what the non-locality theorem needs.

title: Non-Locality of Identity under NFD
label: prop:nonlocality
statement: [Non-Locality of Identity under NFD] Assume Hypotheses~ ref hyp:topo and ref hyp:nfd . Then no canonical finite-time observation determines identity. More precisely, for every t the canonical projection [ p_t: Id to S_t ] is not injective, so identity is not recoverable from any finite slice through the projective observation maps.
statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Non-Locality of Identity under NFD]\label{prop:nonlocality}
Assume Hypotheses~\ref{hyp:topo} and \ref{hyp:nfd}. Then no canonical finite-time observation determines identity. More precisely, for every $t$ the canonical projection
\[
p_t:\Id\to S_t
\]
is not injective, so identity is not recoverable from any finite slice through the projective observation maps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Weighted Product Metric]\label{def:weighted-metric}
For nonempty metric spaces $(S_t,d_t)$ and weights $0<w_t<\infty$, write
\[

 P_b=\{x\in\textstyle\prod_t S_t:d_w(x,b)<\infty\}.
\]
The formula defines an extended metric on the product and an ordinary metric on each finite-distance component $P_b$.
\end{definition}

statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Finiteness, Completeness and Compactness of Weighted Histories]\label{prop:weighted-history}
The formula is finite on every pair in the full product exactly when the weighted diameters are bounded outside a finite set of stages. For finite-diameter stages this is equivalent to $B=\sup_t w_t\operatorname{diam}(S_t)<\infty$. For any nonempty inverse limit $I$ and $b\in I$, it is finite on all of $I$ exactly when $I\subseteq P_b$. If the coordinate spaces are complete and the bonding maps continuous, $P_b$ and $I\cap P_b$ are complete. If $w_t\operatorname{diam}(S_t)\to0$, the weighted metric induces the product topology and
\[
 0\leq d_w(x,y)-\max_{0\leq t\leq N} w_t d_t(x_t,y_t)
 \leq \sup_{t>N} w_t\operatorname{diam}(S_t).
\]
In this case compact coordinate spaces give a compact inverse limit. Surjective bonding maps give a compatible history through each stage point.
\end{proposition}

statement_tex:
\begin{example}[A Ramified Tower with Positive Deformation and Coherent Transport]\label{ex:coherent-rotation-tower}
Take $S_t=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)\times\{0,1\}^{t}$ with the maximum of the circle distance (circumference one) and the discrete prefix distance. Let $\pi_t$ keep the angle and delete the last bit, and take $w_t=2^{-t}$. For an intervention at stage $k$ with amplitude $0<a<1/2$, replace $\pi_k$ by prefix deletion and angle shift $-a$. Set $h_t$ to the identity for $t\leq k$ and to angle shift $a$ for $t>k$. The inverses shift by $-a$ on those same levels. The squares commute at $k$ by cancellation and at every other level by commutation with prefix deletion. Each limit has at least two histories over every finite cut, since a later bit may be flipped.

All bonding maps are $1$-Lipschitz and satisfy the fiber estimate with $K_t=1$: set the required angle and prefix, retaining the last bit. Thus $q_t=1/2$. The chosen dimensionless intervention cost is $E_w=w_k a$, and $\sup_x d_w(x,Hx)=w_{k+1}a=E_w/2$. More precisely, for $b=w_{k+1}$,
\[
 d_H(I,\widetilde I)=\frac{ba}{1+b}>0.
\]
Indeed an original history has constant angle $\theta$ and a perturbed one has angle $\varphi$ up to $k$ and $\varphi+a$ thereafter. If the two histories are at distance $r$, the circle triangle inequality gives $a\leq r+r/b$ from stages $0$ and $k+1$. Choosing identical bits and $\varphi=\theta-ba/(1+b)$ attains equality. That choice is reversible for every perturbed history and gives both directed distances. For the sector of these single jumps the infimum of the cost-to-deformation ratio is $2$, since the ratio is $2(1+b)$ at stage $k$. This uses the declared projection-defect cost. An entropy-based cost requires a separate comparison.
\end{example}

These assignments satisfy E0, controlled E1, and E2, with

statement_tex:
\begin{example}[External Null Witness in a Common Readout Domain]\label{ex:joint-external-null-witness}
Fix $k\geq0$ and $0<a<1/2$. Use the weighted circle-prefix history metric with weights $3^{-t}$, the undeformed tower $I_0$, the single-jump tower $I_1$ (bonding shift $-a$ at level $k$), and $Z=I_0\cup I_1$. Set $\beta=3^{-(k+1)}$. The common readout $F$ takes the initial angle, the angle at $k+1$, and the ternary code of the bits, with codomain metric $\max(\rho_0,\beta\rho_1,|\Delta\text{code}|)$. The two angular blocks give the first two terms of $d_w$, while the ternary leading term minus its tail bounds the binary part from below. Thus $C=1$ holds on the entire compact union. Order the codomain by equality together with $e_0=(0,0,0)$ below every element.

Declare internal interventions to be simultaneous rotations of all stages of $I_0$, with cost the absolute shortest angular shift. Every such map has its inverse and sends $I_0$ onto itself. This gives infinite resistance in this sector by the Hausdorff convention, despite finite-cost nonidentity transports. The pointwise readout changes under a nonzero rotation. A sector admitting the single-jump deformation instead has a finite resistance witness with projection-defect cost $3^{-k}a$. The two sectors specify different admissible operations.

Declare as a separate extension the addition of the single-jump branch to $I_0$. It is the union of two compact projective limits; it is also realized by the disjoint union of the two stage towers with branch-preserving projections. Embed its histories in $Z$ by forgetting the tag, which is injective at the limit since the phases across $k$ distinguish the two branches. The inclusion $j:I_0\hookrightarrow Z$ preserves the restricted readout exactly. Take $z_0=j(x)$ with zero phase and all-zero bits and $z_1$ on the added branch with the same initial phase and bits. Then
\[
 d_Z(z_0,z_1)=\beta a,\qquad F(z_0)=e_0,\qquad
 d_{\mathcal E}(F(z_1),e_0)=\beta a.
\]
The extension is positive in Hausdorff distance, $\beta a/(1+\beta)$, using the two angular blocks. The transported point and the added endpoint are distinct. The scalar ternary readout alone, which discards both angles, assigns them the same value and fails the positive lower bound on this pair. The example realizes a typed extension witness and distinguishes setwise resistance from readout invariance.
\end{example}

\begin{definition}[Witness margin vector]\label{def:margins}
Define the witness margin vector
\[
\Delta(S)=
\bigl(
\delta_{\mathrm{per}}(S),

\delta_{\mathrm{cont}}(S),

\[
\delta_\star(S)=\min\Delta(S).

A positive radius certifies the associated predicate at the target and throughout its declared perturbation ball. A zero or unreported radius alone does not determine failure at the target. Raw separations, risks, durations, fragmentation ceilings and compression errors require separate calibration before taking this minimum.
\end{definition}

statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Causal integration]\label{def:iint}
An admissible system satisfies causal integration, written $\Iint(S)=1$, if there is no non-trivial factorization
\[
\Aset=A_1\times A_2,\qquad R=R_1\sqcup R_2,
\]
together with decomposed dynamics and causal structure reproducing admissible histories within error smaller than a positive margin $\delta_{\mathrm{int}}(S)$ while preserving $\Id_S$.
More explicitly, this shorthand is relative to a declared admissible
factorization class.  For such a class $\mathfrak{D}$, write
$\Iint(S;\mathfrak{D})=1$ when no factorization in $\mathfrak{D}$
reproduces the admissible histories below a positive margin
$\delta_{\mathrm{int}}(S;\mathfrak{D})$ while preserving $\Id_S$.
The unqualified notation $\Iint(S)=1$ refers to the default structural class
$\mathfrak{D}_{\ast}$: fixed, time-homogeneous, schedule-independent,
non-trivial product factorizations with both factors non-singleton, with
split readouts $R=R_1\sqcup R_2$, decomposed dynamics and causal structure, a
search space normalized independently of the target error, and no
reconstruction decoder or time-dependent post-processing map that re-couples
the factors at output time.  This default structural reading is the adopted
class recorded in
\texttt{docs/ai-platform-outputs/analysis/QICN\_IINT\_CANONICAL\_CLASS\_SPLIT\_READOUT.md}.
\end{definition}

title: Class-relative integration margin

In particular, under decoder-coupled or schedule-dependent behavioral classes such as mathfrak D _ mathrm approx , the corresponding margin delta _ mathrm int (S; mathfrak D _ mathrm approx ) may vanish, i.e. may be equal to 0 ; the current coupled-carrier analysis records precisely this failure mode. \begin{remark}[Class-relative integration margin]

statement: [Discrete Transition Operator] Fix auxiliary energy and phase coordinates (e_i)_i and ( phi _i)_i , a graph with incoming neighborhoods operatorname conn (i) , and a control u in U . Write [ C_N=[0,1]^N, qquad d_N^ rm in = max _i| operatorname conn (i)|, qquad d_N^ rm out = max _j| i:j in operatorname conn (i) |. ] The coherence-coordinate transition [ widehat T_ N,u ^ e, phi :C_N to C_N ] is defined componentwise by [ bigl ( widehat T_ N,u ^ e, phi mathbf x bigr )_i = operatorname clamp _ [0,1] ! left ( x_i+ eta R_i( mathbf x ;e, phi )+ alpha ,B_i( mathbf x )+ Gamma _ N,i (u) right ), ] where [ R_i( mathbf x ;e, phi ) = sum _ j in operatorname conn (i) I_j(x_j) frac exp (-|e_i-e_j|/(kT)) theta cos ( phi _i- phi _j) . ] Here I_j:[0,1] to is the intensity readout, B_i is a feedback term, Ga
statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Discrete Transition Operator]
Fix auxiliary energy and phase coordinates $(e_i)_i$ and $(\phi_i)_i$, a graph with incoming neighborhoods $\operatorname{conn}(i)$, and a control $u\in\U$. Write
\[
C_N=[0,1]^N,\qquad
d_N^{\rm in}=\max_i|\operatorname{conn}(i)|,\qquad
d_N^{\rm out}=\max_j|\{i:j\in\operatorname{conn}(i)\}|.
\]
The coherence-coordinate transition
\[
\widehat T_{N,u}^{e,\phi}:C_N\to C_N
\]
is defined componentwise by
\[
\bigl(\widehat T_{N,u}^{e,\phi}\mathbf{x}\bigr)_i
=
\operatorname{clamp}_{[0,1]}\!\left(
x_i+\eta R_i(\mathbf{x};e,\phi)+\alpha\,B_i(\mathbf{x})+\Gamma_{N,i}(u)
\right),
\]
where
\[
R_i(\mathbf{x};e,\phi)
=
\sum_{j\in\operatorname{conn}(i)}
I_j(x_j)
\frac{\exp(-|e_i-e_j|/(kT))}
{\theta\cos(\phi_i-\phi_j)}.
\]
Here $I_j:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ is the intensity readout, $B_i$ is a feedback term, $\Gamma_N(u)$ is the finite input coupling, and $k,T,\theta>0$, $\eta,\alpha\geq0$ are parameters. Energy and phase are frozen in this operator; contractivity of this coordinate map does not establish contractivity of a coupled energy--phase evolution.
\end{definition}

title: Discrete Regularity Conditions
label: ass:discrete-regularity
statement: [Discrete Regularity Conditions] For a fixed parameter region, assume: [leftmargin=*] item I_j is L_I -Lipschitz for every node j . item The phase denominator is uniformly separated from zero: there exists c_ phi >0 such that | cos ( phi _i- phi _j)| ge c_ phi on every active edge. item There exist beta >0 and an L_D -Lipschitz map D:C_N to Hilb _N such that B( mathbf x )=- beta mathbf x +D( mathbf x ) . item Gamma _N(u) is independent of mathbf x for fixed u . item The parameters satisfy [ L_R:= frac L_I sqrt d_N^ rm in d_N^ rm out theta c_ phi , qquad rho _N:=|1- alpha beta |+ eta L_R+ alpha L_D<1. ]
statement_tex:
\begin{assumption}[Discrete Regularity Conditions]\label{ass:discrete-regularity}
For a fixed parameter region, assume:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*]
\item $I_j$ is $L_I$-Lipschitz for every node $j$.
\item The phase denominator is uniformly separated from zero: there exists $c_\phi>0$ such that $|\cos(\phi_i-\phi_j)|\ge c_\phi$ on every active edge.
\item There exist $\beta>0$ and an $L_D$-Lipschitz map $D:C_N\to\Hilb_N$ such that $B(\mathbf{x})=-\beta\mathbf{x}+D(\mathbf{x})$.
\item $\Gamma_N(u)$ is independent of $\mathbf{x}$ for fixed $u$.
\item The parameters satisfy
\[
L_R:=\frac{L_I\sqrt{d_N^{\rm in}d_N^{\rm out}}}{\theta c_\phi},
\qquad
\rho_N:=|1-\alpha\beta|+\eta L_R+\alpha L_D<1.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{assumption}

title: Discrete Operator Contractivity
label: thm:discrete-contraction
statement: [Discrete Operator Contractivity] Under Assumption~ ref ass:discrete-regularity , for fixed u,e, phi the operator widehat T_ N,u ^ e, phi is a strict contraction on the complete set C_N : [ norm widehat T_ N,u ^ e, phi ( mathbf x )- widehat T_ N,u ^ e, phi ( mathbf y ) _N le rho _N norm mathbf x - mathbf y _N qquad forall mathbf x , mathbf y in C_N. ] It has a unique fixed point in C_N , and every iterate starting there converges to it.
statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Discrete Operator Contractivity]\label{thm:discrete-contraction}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:discrete-regularity}, for fixed $u,e,\phi$ the operator $\widehat T_{N,u}^{e,\phi}$ is a strict contraction on the complete set $C_N$:
\[
\norm{\widehat T_{N,u}^{e,\phi}(\mathbf{x})-\widehat T_{N,u}^{e,\phi}(\mathbf{y})}_N
\le
\rho_N\norm{\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}}_N
\qquad
\forall \mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}\in C_N.
\]
It has a unique fixed point in $C_N$, and every iterate starting there converges to it.
\end{theorem}

title: Convergence of Fixed Points

statement: [Convergence of Fixed Points] Let f_u^ ast and widehat f_ N,u ^ ast be the unique fixed points of T_u and widehat T_ N,u ^ e, phi . Under the assumptions of Theorem~ ref thm:bridge , [ norm J_N widehat f_ N,u ^ ast -f_u^ ast _ Hilb le frac eps _N 1- kappa . ] Consequently, for a fixed kappa <1 , if eps _N to 0 , then [ lim _ N to infty norm J_N widehat f_ N,u ^ ast -f_u^ ast _ Hilb =0. ]

statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Realized Contractive Bridge with Nonconstant Equilibria]\label{thm:realized-nonconstant-bridge}
Let $0<\kappa<1$, let $\U$ be a nonempty compact interval, and let a nonconstant Lipschitz profile $a:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfy
\[
0\leq a(s)+u\leq1-\kappa\qquad(s\in[0,1],\ u\in\U).
\]
Take $\I=C$, $Kf=\kappa\int_0^1f$, and $\Gamma(u)(s)=a(s)+u$. Let $a_{N,i}=N\int_{I_{N,i}}a$ and
\[
\widehat T_{N,u}(\mathbf{x})_i
=\operatorname{clamp}_{[0,1]}\left(\kappa\frac1N\sum_jx_j+a_{N,i}+u\right).
\]
This finite transition has the original increment form: choose all $N$ nodes as incoming neighbors (including self-edges), $I_j(x_j)=x_j$, $e_i=\phi_i=0$, $k=T=1$, $\theta=N/\kappa$, $\eta=\alpha=\beta=1$, $D=0$, $B(\mathbf{x})=-\mathbf{x}$ and $\Gamma_{N,i}=a_{N,i}+u$. The assumptions of the discrete contraction and bridge theorems hold with $\rho_N=\kappa$ and
\[
\eps_N=\norm{P_Na-a}\leq\frac{L_a}{\sqrt{12}\,N}.
\]
Writing $\bar a=\int_0^1a$, the equilibria are
\[
f_u^\ast(s)=a(s)+u+\kappa\frac{\bar a+u}{1-\kappa},\qquad
\widehat f_{N,u,i}^\ast=a_{N,i}+u+\kappa\frac{\bar a+u}{1-\kappa}.
\]
In particular, H1--H5 hold and
\[
\norm{J_N\widehat f_{N,u}^\ast-f_u^\ast}
=\norm{P_Na-a}\leq\frac{L_a}{\sqrt{12}\,N},\qquad
\dist(f_u^\ast,\mathcal N)=\norm{a-\bar a}>0.
\]
These conclusions hold simultaneously for every $u\in\U$.
\end{theorem}

The stage maps commute with their bonding maps and with the existing transport $h_t$ between towers. At fixed $u$, the map $D_{s,u}$ has sharp Lipschitz constant $1/3$ on $I_s$ in $d_w$. The existing transport $H$ conjugates the two evolutions and sends $x^\ast_{0,u}$ to $x^\ast_{1,u}$. Their $d_w$ and common readout distances are both $\beta_k a$. The finite readouts retain E0--E2 on each history domain, with the original uniform tail $3^{-t}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hilbert Realization of the Projective Dissipation]\label{thm:hilbert-projective-dissipation}
The circle-prefix evolutions above embed into the BaseCore projected dynamics on $L^2([0,1])$ with $C=\{0\leq f\leq1\text{ a.e.}\}$, $\|K\|=1/3$, and compact parameter space $\{0,1\}\times\mathbb T$. The embedding is bi-Lipschitz on $I_0\cup I_1$ for fixed $k$. The equilibrium profiles $f^\ast_{s,u}$ satisfy
\[
 \inf_{s,u}\operatorname{dist}(f^\ast_{s,u},\mathcal N)\geq\sqrt{2/45},
\]
where $\mathcal N$ is the subspace of constant $L^2$ functions. Thus H5 follows for this family.

At depth $t$ let $Q_t$ be the orthogonal projection onto the retained profile cells, with zero tail. The realized finite map has $N_t=8\cdot 9^t$ equal-mesh nodes and its embedded update is $Q_tT_{s,u}$. It commutes with restriction in the sense $Q_tT_{s,u}=Q_tT_{s,u}Q_t$ on $C$. Its uniform one-step discrepancy on $C$ is at most $3^{-t}/\sqrt{2}$, with equality for $t\geq1$. Its fixed point is $Q_tf^\ast_{s,u}$, with error at most the same bound. Starting the finite evolution at $Q_tf_0$ gives this bound at every iteration $n\geq1$ relative to the orbit from $f_0$.
\end{theorem}

statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Operational Self-Reference $\Sigmaop$]\label{def:sigma-op}
An admissible system $S$ admits operational self-reference, written $\Sigmaop(S)=1$, if there exists a map
\[
\Sigma:\Aset\to\Aset
\]
and constants $\eps_\Sigma\ge 0$ and $0\le L_\Sigma<1$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{Approximate self-accuracy:} for every $x\in\Aset$,
\[
d_X(\Sigma(x),x)\le \eps_\Sigma.
\]
\item \textbf{Contractive stabilization:}
\[
d_X(\Sigma(x),\Sigma(y))\le L_\Sigma d_X(x,y)
\quad\text{for all }x,y\in\Aset.
\]
\item \textbf{Intervention commutation:} for every admissible intervention $u\in U$,
\[
\Sigma\circ \Phi_u = \Phi_u\circ \Sigma
\quad\text{on }\Aset.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Any such $\Sigma$ is called a contractive admissible self-model.
\end{definition}

statement: [Fibre Truncation Has a Sharp Commutation Defect] On the tower (p, theta ,b) with c(b)= sum _ j ge 1 2b_j3^ -j , fix m ge 1 and let b^ star =(0,1,0,1, ldots ) . statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Fibre Truncation Has a Sharp Commutation Defect]\label{prop:sigma-fibre-truncation}
On the tower $(p,\theta,b)$ with $c(b)=\sum_{j\ge1}2b_j3^{-j}$, fix $m\ge1$ and let $b^\star=(0,1,0,1,\ldots)$. The truncation $T_m$ fixes $p,\theta,b_1,\ldots,b_m$ and fills the tail with that of $b^\star$. In the metric $\max\{\mathbf1_{p\ne p'},\rho(\theta,\theta'),|c(b)-c(b')|\}$ it has uniform approximation error at most $3^{-m}$ and Lipschitz constant zero within every fibre of the retained data. For $\Phi_{u,q}(p,\theta,b)=(p,u+q\lambda b_1,Rb)$ with $Rb=(0,1-b_1,1-b_2,\ldots)$, its pointwise commutation defect is
\[
 d(T_m\Phi_{u,q}x,\Phi_{u,q}T_m x)
 =2\,3^{-(m+1)}\,\mathbf1_{b_m\ne b^\star_m}.
\]
In particular the uniform defect is exactly $2\,3^{-(m+1)}$.
\end{proposition}

title: $\Cop \to$ Partial Operational Subjecthood
label: thm:main-partial-subjecthood
statement: [ Cop to Partial Operational Subjecthood] Let S be an admissible system with S in Cop . Then: [leftmargin=1.5em] item S satisfies Piop . item S satisfies Iotaop . item Qop (S) is well-defined. item S satisfies weak non-null Phiop on admissible support. item Sigmaop is not implied by Cop ; it requires the independent hypothesis Sigma 1 . item Subbridge requires Sigma 1 in addition to Cop and therefore is a subclass of Cop .
statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[$\Cop \to$ Partial Operational Subjecthood]\label{thm:main-partial-subjecthood}
Let $S$ be an admissible system with $S\in\Cop$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item $S$ satisfies $\Piop$.
\item $S$ satisfies $\Iotaop$.
\item $\Qop(S)$ is well-defined.
\item $S$ satisfies weak non-null $\Phiop$ on admissible support.
\item $\Sigmaop$ is not implied by $\Cop$; it requires the independent hypothesis $\Sigma1$.
\item $\Subbridge$ requires $\Sigma1$ in addition to $\Cop$ and therefore is a subclass of $\Cop$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Finiteness, Completeness and Compactness of Weighted Histories]\label{prop:weighted-history}
The formula is finite on every pair in the full product exactly when the weighted diameters are bounded outside a finite set of stages. For finite-diameter stages this is equivalent to $B=\sup_t w_t\operatorname{diam}(S_t)<\infty$. For any nonempty inverse limit $I$ and $b\in I$, it is finite on all of $I$ exactly when $I\subseteq P_b$. If the coordinate spaces are complete and the bonding maps continuous, $P_b$ and $I\cap P_b$ are complete. If $w_t\operatorname{diam}(S_t)\to0$, the weighted metric induces the product topology and
\[
 0\leq d_w(x,y)-\max_{0\leq t\leq N} w_t d_t(x_t,y_t)
 \leq \sup_{t>N} w_t\operatorname{diam}(S_t).
\]
In this case compact coordinate spaces give a compact inverse limit. Surjective bonding maps give a compatible history through each stage point.
\end{proposition}

statement_tex:
\begin{example}[A Ramified Tower with Positive Deformation and Coherent Transport]\label{ex:coherent-rotation-tower}
Take $S_t=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)\times\{0,1\}^{t}$ with the maximum of the circle distance (circumference one) and the discrete prefix distance. Let $\pi_t$ keep the angle and delete the last bit, and take $w_t=2^{-t}$. For an intervention at stage $k$ with amplitude $0<a<1/2$, replace $\pi_k$ by prefix deletion and angle shift $-a$. Set $h_t$ to the identity for $t\leq k$ and to angle shift $a$ for $t>k$. The inverses shift by $-a$ on those same levels. The squares commute at $k$ by cancellation and at every other level by commutation with prefix deletion. Each limit has at least two histories over every finite cut, since a later bit may be flipped.

All bonding maps are $1$-Lipschitz and satisfy the fiber estimate with $K_t=1$: set the required angle and prefix, retaining the last bit. Thus $q_t=1/2$. For this example set the dimensionless intervention cost $E_w=D_w=w_k a$, and $\sup_x d_w(x,Hx)=w_{k+1}a=E_w/2$. More precisely, for $b=w_{k+1}$,
\[
 d_H(I,\widetilde I)=\frac{ba}{1+b}>0.
\]
Indeed an original history has constant angle $\theta$ and a perturbed one has angle $\varphi$ up to $k$ and $\varphi+a$ thereafter. If the two histories are at distance $r$, the circle triangle inequality gives $a\leq r+r/b$ from stages $0$ and $k+1$. Choosing identical bits and $\varphi=\theta-ba/(1+b)$ attains equality. That choice is reversible for every perturbed history and gives both directed distances. For the sector of these single jumps the infimum of the cost-to-deformation ratio is $2$, since the ratio is $2(1+b)$ at stage $k$. This uses the declared projection-defect cost. An entropy-based cost requires a separate comparison.
\end{example}

\begin{theorem}[Resistance under Audited Transport]\label{thm:non-transferability}
Let an ambient bijection $A$ satisfy $c\,d(x,y)\leq d'(Ax,Ay)\leq C\,d(x,y)$ with $0<c\leq C<\infty$. It maps the baseline identity to the target identity. Suppose a bijection between the declared intervention sectors maps $\delta$ to $\delta'$ with $A(I_\delta)=I'_{\delta'}$ and $a E(\delta)\leq E'(\delta')\leq b E(\delta)$ for $0<a\leq b<\infty$. For nonempty baseline and deformed sets at finite Hausdorff distance, the two resistance values satisfy
\[
 \frac{a}{C}M_\Omega\leq M'_\Omega\leq\frac{b}{c}M_\Omega.
\]
In particular such a transport preserves the finite versus infinite resistance class.
\end{theorem}

\[

\qquad

\[

\]

\[
d_{\mathcal I}(b,c)\leq|\Phi(b)-\Phi(c)|\leq3d_{\mathcal I}(b,c).
\]
The domain is compact and complete, and the readout is injective and bi-Lipschitz onto its image. Thus a global lower bound is realized here rather than inserted without a witness.

\begin{theorem}[Continuity and Conditional Perturbation Invariance]\label{thm:forced-continuity}
Under E1, if each finite readout $g_n=\phi_n\circ p_n$ is continuous, then $\Phi$ is continuous, irrespective of $M_\Omega$. Under the zero-displacement branch of Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:audited-comparison},

\begin{example}[Nonempty Assignment and Null-Anchored Witness]\label{ex:null-realization}
Let $Z=\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}$, let $d_Z(x,y)=3^{-(m+1)}$ at their first differing bit $m$, and let $\E=[0,1]$ with its usual order, metric and null $0$. Set $d_Z(x,x)=0$. The ternary readout $F(b)=\sum_{j\geq0}2b_j/3^{j+1}$ satisfies
\[
d_Z(x,y)\leq |F(x)-F(y)|\leq3d_Z(x,y).
\]
The first differing term has magnitude $2/3^{m+1}$ and the remaining tail is at most $1/3^{m+1}$, proving both bounds. The all-zero and all-one sequences give images $0$ and $1$, a null-anchored pair. Every finite prefix has different readout completions, while uniform tail error is $3^{-(N+1)}$; thus the revised E1 and E2 are realized together. The finite positive witness image $\{1\}$ has relative gap one, but the ambient global lower gap at $1$ is zero. This model supplies readout geometry, not an infinite-mass cost certificate or phenomenal evidence.
\end{example}

statement_tex:
\begin{example}[External Null Witness in a Common Readout Domain]\label{ex:joint-external-null-witness}
Fix $k\geq0$ and $0<a<1/2$. Use the weighted circle-prefix history metric with weights $3^{-t}$, the undeformed tower $I_0$, the single-jump tower $I_1$ (bonding shift $-a$ at level $k$), and $Z=I_0\cup I_1$. Set $\beta=3^{-(k+1)}$. The common readout $F$ takes the initial angle, the angle at $k+1$, and the ternary code of the bits, with codomain metric $\max(\rho_0,\beta\rho_1,|\Delta\text{code}|)$. The two angular blocks give the first two terms of $d_w$, while the ternary leading term minus its tail bounds the binary part from below. Thus $C=1$ holds on the entire compact union. Order the codomain by equality together with $e_0=(0,0,0)$ below every element.

Declare internal interventions to be simultaneous rotations of all stages of $I_0$, with cost the absolute shortest angular shift. Every such map has its inverse and sends $I_0$ onto itself. This gives infinite resistance in this sector by the Hausdorff convention, despite finite-cost nonidentity transports. The pointwise readout changes under a nonzero rotation. A sector admitting the single-jump deformation instead has a finite resistance witness with projection-defect cost $3^{-k}a$. The two sectors specify different admissible operations.

Declare as a separate extension the addition of the single-jump branch to $I_0$. It is the union of two compact projective limits; it is also realized by the disjoint union of the two stage towers with branch-preserving projections. Embed its histories in $Z$ by forgetting the tag, which is injective at the limit since the phases across $k$ distinguish the two branches. The inclusion $j:I_0\hookrightarrow Z$ preserves the restricted readout exactly. Take $z_0=j(x)$ with zero phase and all-zero bits and $z_1$ on the added branch with the same initial phase and bits. Then
\[
 d_Z(z_0,z_1)=\beta a,\qquad F(z_0)=e_0,\qquad
 d_{\mathcal E}(F(z_1),e_0)=\beta a.
\]
The extension is positive in Hausdorff distance, $\beta a/(1+\beta)$, using the two angular blocks. The transported point and the added endpoint are distinct. The scalar ternary readout alone, which discards both angles, assigns them the same value and fails the positive lower bound on this pair. The example realizes a typed extension witness and distinguishes setwise resistance from readout invariance.
\end{example}

\begin{definition}[Admissible system]\label{def:system}
An admissible system in this paper is a tuple
\[
S = (X,\Phi,C,R,\Gamma,U)
\]
with the following components:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item $X$ is a metrizable internal state space with metric $d_X$.
\item $\Phi = \{\Phi_u\}_{u \in U}$ is a family of admissible transition operators $\Phi_u : X \to X$ indexed by interventions.
\item $C$ is the effective causal structure of the system: the object that records which factorizations, intervention responses, and couplings are admissible on $X$.
\item $R = \{r_\alpha\}_{\alpha \in \Lambda_R}$ is a family of internal or external readouts, each $r_\alpha : X \to Y_\alpha$.
\item $\Gamma = \{\gamma_j\}_{j=1}^m$ is the admissibility bundle. Each $\gamma_j$ is a constraint functional; the admissible region is
\[
X_\Gamma = \{x \in X : \gamma_j(x) \le 0 \ \forall j\}.
\]
\item $U$ is the set of admissible interventions, already filtered by the corpus-level governance requirement that interventions remain auditable, comparable, and methodologically bounded.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Positive Split-Readout Margin on the Cofinal Tower]\label{thm:circle-prefix-cofinal-margin}
Keep $Z$ and the same three readout channels. Enlarge the control by $q\in\{-1,0,1\}$ and fix $0<\lambda\le1/9$. On branch $s$ set
\[
 \Psi_{u,q}(s,\theta,b)=(s,u+q\lambda b_1,R(b)).
\]
These maps descend to all stages $t\ge1$ and commute with the jump transport, with the same inverse-limit support and the same E1--E2 readout. Each branch is forward invariant and each fixed-control map has sharp contraction factor $1/3$ there. The sector of product encodings and split-readout approximants just declared is nonempty. Its infimal error $e_\ast$ satisfies
\[
 \frac{\beta\lambda}{2}\ \le\ e_\ast\ \le\ \frac{\lambda}{2}.
\]
For comparators reproducing all three channels exactly at time zero, the infimal error is exactly $\lambda/2$. At $\lambda=0$ the original exact comparator is recovered. For $\lambda>0$, the new controls fail to descend to depth zero.
\end{theorem}

statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Legibility of Matched Integration Responses]\label{thm:matched-integration-legibility}
Use the windows of Definition~\ref{def:matched-paired-response-window} with $\lambda\in\{0\}\cup[L,1/9]$ and adversarial observation error at most $\eta=1/256$ in the paired metric. The following are the L1--L6 properties of Definition~\ref{def:ileg} evaluated on the paired-response domain.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item The clean high and low response sets have separation exactly $L$.
\item All observations in the allowed noise balls preserve the clean class, with zero abstentions.
\item For any train of at least three freshly reset pairs at a fixed coupling and fixed prepared first bit, the class persists when the common input phase varies across pairs.
\item In the nonempty target population, retain the same state and common input, prepare $b_1=1$, and ablate $\lambda\in[L,1/9]$ to zero between paired trials. The class changes from high to low with zero misses.
\item In the nonempty sham population, retain the state and coupling and vary the common input across paired trials. Both first-bit strata are allowed. The false-change and abstention rates are zero.
\item On the resolved domain one bit retains the class with zero discrete class distortion, and zero bits are insufficient. Including the audit status of abstention requires two bits in a fixed-length encoding.
\end{enumerate}
At error radius $L/2$ a low and a high experiment can have identical full observations. If the common-input condition is removed, even a noise-free uncoupled experiment can decode as high.
\end{theorem}

title: Exact and approximate structural equivalence
label: def:equiv
statement: [Exact and approximate structural equivalence] Fix eps ge 0 . We write [ S_1 simeq _ ( Gamma , eps ) S_2 ] if there exists a structural equivalence datum ( chi , upsilon , rho ) such that: [leftmargin=1.5em] item textbf Dynamic intertwining: [ sup _ x in A_1, u in U_1, 0 le t le T_ Gamma d_ X_2 ! left ( chi ( Phi _ 1,u ^t(x)), Phi _ 2, upsilon (u) ^t( chi (x)) right ) le eps . ] item textbf Readout compatibility: [ sup _ x,u,t, alpha left | r^ (1) _ alpha ( Phi _ 1,u ^t(x)) - rho (r^ (1) _ alpha )( Phi _ 2, upsilon (u) ^t( chi (x))) right | le eps . ] item textbf Admissibility preservation: admissible trajectories in S_1 map to admissible trajectories in S_2 and conversely. item textbf Invariant preservation: the witness margins for all six invariants differ by at most eps . item textbf Pa
statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Exact and approximate structural equivalence]\label{def:equiv}
Fix $\eps \ge 0$. We write
\[
S_1 \simeq_{(\Gamma,\eps)} S_2
\]
if there exists a structural equivalence datum $(\chi,\upsilon,\rho)$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{Dynamic intertwining:}
\[
\sup_{x \in A_1,\ u \in U_1,\ 0 \le t \le T_\Gamma}
d_{X_2}\!\left(\chi(\Phi_{1,u}^t(x)), \Phi_{2,\upsilon(u)}^t(\chi(x))\right) \le \eps.
\]
\item \textbf{Readout compatibility:}
\[
\sup_{x,u,t,\alpha}
\left|
r^{(1)}_\alpha(\Phi_{1,u}^t(x))
-
\rho(r^{(1)}_\alpha)(\Phi_{2,\upsilon(u)}^t(\chi(x)))
\right|
\le \eps.
\]
\item \textbf{Admissibility preservation:} admissible trajectories in $S_1$ map to admissible trajectories in $S_2$ and conversely.
\item \textbf{Invariant preservation:} the witness margins for all six invariants differ by at most $\eps$.
\item \textbf{Partition preservation:}
\[
x \sim_{Q,S_1} y \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \chi(x) \sim_{Q,S_2} \chi(y).
\]
\end{enumerate}
The case $\eps=0$ is called \emph{exact} structural equivalence and written $S_1 \simeq_{\Gamma} S_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Rupture]\label{def:rupture}
Given $S$, a rupture is any loss of admissibility or loss of at least one critical invariant margin beyond its admissible threshold. Ruptures are classified as:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{persistence rupture} (support loss or collapse exposure),
\item \textbf{identity rupture} (loss of unique rigid identity),
\item \textbf{integration rupture} (reducible factorization),
\item \textbf{continuity rupture} (fragmentation into incompatible classes),
\item \textbf{differentiation rupture} (null or trivial collapse),
\item \textbf{legibility rupture} (decoder, noise, or negative-control failure).
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Approximate margin preservation]\label{prop:margins}
If $S_1 \simeq_{(\Gamma,\eps)} S_2$ with margins calibrated in a common perturbation metric for both systems, then for every critical invariant index $j$,
\[
\bigl| \delta_j(S_1) - \delta_j(S_2) \bigr| \le \eps.
\]
Hence
\[
\delta_\star(S_2) \ge \delta_\star(S_1) - \eps.
\]
\end{proposition}

statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Approximate stability]\label{thm:stability}
Let $S_1 \in \Cop$ and suppose both systems use certified radii in the same perturbation metric, with
\[

=

\[

\]

title: Conditional Use of Single-Rupture Schemas
label: thm:six-witness-schemas
statement: [Conditional Use of Single-Rupture Schemas] Consider these six candidate schemas. A schema separates its target invariant from the other five only when an admissible model realizes the five retained predicates and fails the target on the same declared comparison domain: [leftmargin=1.5em] item textbf Persistence witness. A system with a certified decoder, non-factorizable causal structure, unique identity label, continuous class map, and non-null differentiation, but whose admissible support exits the declared forward-invariant domain under some u in U . item textbf Rigid-identity witness. A system with persistent support, integration, continuity, differentiation, and legibility, but with two compatible non-isomorphic identity candidates transported by the same readout family. item textbf
statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Conditional Use of Single-Rupture Schemas]\label{thm:six-witness-schemas}
Consider these six candidate schemas. A schema separates its target invariant
from the other five only when an admissible model realizes the five retained
predicates and fails the target on the same declared comparison domain:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{Persistence witness.} A system with a certified decoder,
non-factorizable causal structure, unique identity label, continuous class map,
and non-null differentiation, but whose admissible support exits the declared
forward-invariant domain under some $u\in U$.
\item \textbf{Rigid-identity witness.} A system with persistent support,
integration, continuity, differentiation, and legibility, but with two
compatible non-isomorphic identity candidates transported by the same readout
family.
\item \textbf{Integration witness.} A product system
$A_S=A_1\times A_2$ with persistent factors, unique factor identities,
continuous dynamics, non-null differentiation, and certified decoders, but with
decoupled intervention histories so that the aggregate factorizes.
\item \textbf{Continuity witness.} A system with persistent support, unique
identity, non-factorizable structure, non-null differentiation, and certified
decoders, but with an admissible transition producing a jump between
incompatible regime classes.
\item \textbf{Differentiation witness.} A persistent, rigid, integrated,
continuous, and legible system whose decoder-visible classes collapse to a
stable null or single indistinguishable class.
\item \textbf{Legibility witness.} A persistent, rigid, integrated, continuous,
and non-null differentiated system whose class partition is latent but no
certified decoder satisfies L1--L6.
\end{enumerate}
Existence of the six models is a separate obligation.
\end{theorem}

statement_tex:
\begin{criterion}[Legibility certificate]\label{crit:legibility}
An operational partition candidate $\pi_{S,T}$ is certified only if:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{Comparator separability}: the induced classes remain distinguishable against pre-registered comparators and ablation baselines.
\item \textbf{Noise robustness}: admissible sensor, channel, or readout perturbations do not dissolve the class map below the legibility margin.
\item \textbf{Persistence window}: the same class assignment survives on windows of length at least $\tau_{\min}(S)$.
\item \textbf{Intervention fidelity}: certified interventions on an invariant induce the predicted directional class change.
\item \textbf{Negative controls}: sham or off-target interventions do not generate the same class signature.
\item \textbf{Structured compressibility}: audit-friendly compression or packetization preserves class structure without total collapse.
\end{enumerate}
\end{criterion}

\begin{definition}[Operational boundary]
An admissible system $S$ has an operational boundary on horizon $\tau$ if there exist disjoint admissible intervention families $\mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{in}},\mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{out}} \subseteq U^\tau$ and a boundary-sensitive readout family $R_{\partial}\subseteq R$ such that

D_{\partial}\!\left(\trace_{S,\tau}(x_0;u_\bullet),\trace_{S,\tau}(x_0;\mathbf{0})\right)
>0
\]
uniformly on $x_0\in\Aset$, where $D_{\partial}$ is a readout distance induced by $R_{\partial}$.

The emph class margin of S for mathcal K is [ M_ mathcal K (S, tau ) := min _i bigl ( Pi _ mathcal K PsiVec _ tau (S)_i- theta _ mathcal K ,i bigr ). ] A system lies in the interior of class mathcal K if M_ mathcal K (S, tau )>0 , on the operational boundary if M_ mathcal K (S, tau ) approx 0 , and outside if M_ mathcal K (S, tau )<0 .
statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Class margin functional]
Let $\theta_{\mathcal{K}}$ be the vector of thresholds relevant to class $\mathcal{K}$. The \emph{class margin} of $S$ for $\mathcal{K}$ is
\[
M_{\mathcal{K}}(S,\tau)
:=
\min_i \bigl(\Pi_{\mathcal{K}}\PsiVec_\tau(S)_i-\theta_{\mathcal{K},i}\bigr).
\]
A system lies in the interior of class $\mathcal{K}$ if $M_{\mathcal{K}}(S,\tau)>0$, on the operational boundary if $M_{\mathcal{K}}(S,\tau)\approx 0$, and outside if $M_{\mathcal{K}}(S,\tau)<0$.
\end{definition}
